overview.en: The V-Moth is a geometrid whose British populations are often found around cultivated fruit bushes.
overview.fr: Le Damas cendré est un papillon géomètre dont les populations britanniques fréquentent souvent les cultures de petits fruits.

identification.en: UKMoths gives an adult wingspan of 25–30 mm.
identification.fr: UKMoths indique une envergure adulte de 25 à 30 mm.

habitat.en: It favours gardens, allotments and other cultivated places where currants or gooseberries grow.
habitat.fr: Il fréquente les jardins, jardins familiaux et autres lieux cultivés où poussent groseilliers ou cassissiers.

diet.en: The caterpillars feed on several currants and gooseberries in the genus Ribes.
diet.fr: Les chenilles se nourrissent de plusieurs groseilliers et cassissiers du genre Ribes.

behavior.en: In central Europe, adults mainly fly in June and July, rarely in late May or early August.
behavior.fr: En Europe centrale, les adultes volent surtout en juin et juillet, rarement à la fin mai ou au début août.

reproduction.en: The egg overwinters, and caterpillars are usually found from mid-April to early June.
reproduction.fr: L’œuf hiverne et les chenilles sont généralement observées de la mi-avril au début juin.

ecology.en: Unlike the conifer-feeding Macaria liturata and Macaria signaria, its caterpillars use Ribes shrubs, often grown in gardens.
ecology.fr: Contrairement aux chenilles de Macaria liturata et Macaria signaria, qui consomment des conifères, les siennes utilisent des arbustes Ribes souvent cultivés dans les jardins.

conservation.en: UKMoths reports that it appears to be declining in Britain, although it remains widely distributed there.
conservation.fr: UKMoths indique que l’espèce semble décliner en Grande-Bretagne, tout en restant largement répartie dans le pays.

facts: UKMoths reports 25–30 mm wingspan, apparent decline but wide British distribution, cultivated fruit areas, adult July–August flight and Ribes hosts; its account does not give clutch details.

uncertainties: The catalogue retains Macaria wauaria, but a 2025 phylogenomic revision reinstated Speranza as a valid genus and published the combination Speranza wauaria; some British references still use Macaria wauaria.
British/European natural-history sources cited here do not establish a global population trend.
review_note: Compared UKMoths with a European ecology account and checked the genus transfer against LepiWiki and the 2025 phylogenomic revision; catalogue spelling is retained.
